title: Boss: the permissions auditor
summary: Apply symbolic chmod, decide access like the kernel, and flag dangerous files.

steps.title: Security review
steps.body: Before go-live, security wants an audit of the app server's files. Each file comes as `ls -l`-style data: a 9-character mode like `rwxr-x---`, an owner and a group.

steps.title: Apply symbolic chmod
steps.prompt: Write `string ApplyChmod(string mode, string spec)`. `mode` is 9 characters (`rw-r-----`), `spec` is comma-separated clauses like `u+x`, `go-w`, `a=r`, `o=` (who letters from `ugoa`, op `+ - =`, perms from `rwx`, possibly empty after `=`). Return the new 9-character mode.
hints: Find the operator with `IndexOfAny`; what's before it is *who*, what's after is the perms.
`=` sets every one of the three positions: listed ones on, the others off.

steps.title: Can this user do that?
prompt: Write `bool CanAccess(string mode, string owner, string group, string user, List<string> userGroups, char want)` where `want` is `'r'`, `'w'` or `'x'`. Follow the kernel's rule: use the **owner** triple if `user == owner`, else the **group** triple if `userGroups` contains `group`, else **other**. Only one triple is ever checked, even if a later one would allow it.
`root` may always read and write, and may execute if **any** triple has `x`.
starter: bool CanAccess(string mode, string owner, string group, string user, List<string> userGroups, char want)
solution: bool CanAccess(string mode, string owner, string group, string user, List<string> userGroups, char want)
hints: Pick the offset 0, 3 or 6 first, then add 0/1/2 for r/w/x.
The owner triple wins even when it is *more* restrictive than group or other.
template: Dojo.Eq("owner may write", true, CanAccess("rw-r-----", "ana", "devs", "ana", dojoNone, 'w'));
Dojo.Eq("group may read", true, CanAccess("rw-r-----", "ana", "devs", "bob", new List<string> { "devs" }, 'r'));
Dojo.Eq("other gets nothing", false, CanAccess("rw-r-----", "ana", "devs", "eve", dojoNone, 'r'));
Dojo.Eq("owner triple wins even if stricter", false, CanAccess("---rwxrwx", "ana", "devs", "ana", dojoNone, 'r'));
Dojo.Eq("root reads anything", true, CanAccess("---------", "ana", "devs", "root", dojoNone, 'r'));
Dojo.Eq("root cannot run non-executables", false, CanAccess("rw-rw-rw-", "ana", "devs", "root", dojoNone, 'x'));

steps.title: Audit report
prompt: Write `List<string> Audit(List<(string Path, string Mode, string Owner)> files)` returning one finding per problem, in input order, formatted `"<path>: <problem>"`:
- `secret readable by others` if the path ends in `.pem`, `.key` or `.env`, or contains `/.ssh/`, and group or other has **any** permission,
- `not owned by root` if the path starts with `/etc/` and the owner isn't `root`.
A file can produce several findings; list them in the order above.
starter: List<string> Audit(List<(string Path, string Mode, string Owner)> files)
solution: List<string> Audit(List<(string Path, string Mode, string Owner)> files)
bool secret = path.EndsWith(".pem") || path.EndsWith(".key") || path.EndsWith(".env") || path.Contains("/.ssh/");
if (secret && mode.Substring(3) != "------") findings.Add($"{path}: secret readable by others");
if (path.StartsWith("/etc/") && owner != "root") findings.Add($"{path}: not owned by root");
hints: Other's `w` is index 7 of the 9-character mode.
Group and other are `mode.Substring(3)`; for a secret it must be `------`.
template: var dojoFiles = new List<(string Path, string Mode, string Owner)> {

Dojo.Eq("findings", new List<string> { "/srv/app/.env: secret readable by others", "/tmp/upload: world-writable", "/etc/nginx/nginx.conf: world-writable", "/etc/nginx/nginx.conf: not owned by root" }, Audit(dojoFiles));
